top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) is the only slate proposal where maturity, mechanistic evidence and attribution are all settled: amine binding, deprotonation and the hard C-N reductive elimination are understood quantitatively, ligand design is transferable, four decades of independent use are visible in synthesis, and credit is a clean two-person split. Its weakness is overlap with the 2010 prize and Kosugi/Migita precedent, handled by wording the citation as general, ligand-controlled catalysis. Targeted degradation ranks second as the larger new capability with a directly measured readout but a contestable three-name cut and no approved degrader; phase separation third because in-cell functional relevance is not yet separated from artefacts; folding landscapes fourth on credit and theory-experiment pairing; no award last.
